title: VoteReady: Digital Checklist for Canadian Voters
description: An engaging game designed to educate Canadians about voting procedures, eligibility, and the importance of civic participation.

title: Ask Eager Beaver
description: A civic engagement tool on YouCount.ca that allows Canadians to ask and upvote questions about government, democracy, and representation — bridging citizens and policymakers.

title: VoteMatch
description: An interactive quiz that helps Canadians discover which party platforms align most closely with their values and priorities.

title: CivicEngage Mobile App
description: An innovative civic technology project by Chloe Sepulveda that integrates a live candidate dashboard and an iOS app designed to make political information more engaging and accessible. The platform combines personalized quizzes, live civic updates, and gamified learning tools to enhance democratic participation and awareness among Canadians.

title: Canadians and Civic Issues: An Analysis of 2021 Canadian Election Study Data
description: A data-driven exploration of civic participation, political trust, and voting behavior in Canada based on the 2021 Canadian Election Study.

title: E-Journal Data
description: An interactive mix of PDFs and embedded dashboards offering analytical insights across Canadian electoral and civic engagement datasets.

title: Understanding Local Governance in Canada
description: Detailed examination of unique characteristics of local governance models within each province and territory in Canada.

title: Election Data Explorer
description: A dataset and dashboard hybrid that visualizes electoral data, voter turnout, and regional voting trends across Canada.

title: Elections Contributions and Outcomes
description: An analysis of campaign donation data in Canadian elections by Carmen Y through the Canada Summer Jobs program, exploring links between fundraising and results.

title: Canadian Federal Election Results Visualization
description: A visual exploration of Canadian federal election results, highlighting seat distributions, turnout rates, and historical changes.

title: 2025 Federal Elections Candidates Database
description: A comprehensive database of candidates running in the 2025 Canadian federal elections, including profiles, party affiliations, and electoral districts.

title: 2025 Post-Election Analysis
description: An analytical report examining the outcomes of the 2025 Canadian federal elections, voter turnout, and implications for future political trends.

title: Overseas Canadians Voting e-Toolkit
description: Comprehensive toolkit designed to assist Canadians living abroad with voting procedures. Includes step-by-step instructions, timelines, and downloadable resources.

title: Understanding Federalism in Canada
description: A comprehensive analysis of Canadian federalism, exploring the constitutional division of powers between federal and provincial governments.

title: Canadians and Civic Issues: An Analysis of 2019 Canadian Election Study Data
description: An analytical report examining civic engagement and political awareness among Canadians using C-DEM's 2019 Canadian Election Study data.

title: Vancouver Regional Showcase
description: An in-person civic engagement showcase held in Vancouver, featuring MPs, MPPs, researchers, and community leaders discussing electoral participation, youth engagement, and civic literacy in Western Canada.

title: Calgary Regional Showcase
description: A live regional event in Calgary spotlighting civic dialogue between policymakers, academics, and youth. The showcase emphasized federal–provincial collaboration, representation, and accessible participation in democratic processes.

title: Winnipeg Regional Showcase
description: An in-person showcase in Winnipeg convening MPs, MPPs, community advocates, and emerging scholars to discuss the evolution of Canada's electoral landscape and civic education initiatives across the Prairies.

title: Voices from Arctic Communities
description: A virtual panel featuring Arctic community leaders discussing the unique challenges and opportunities for civic engagement and electoral participation in Northern Canada.

title: Education and Community in the North: Lessons from Fort Resolution
description: A virtual discussion with Deninu School Principal Simone Degannes-Lange, exploring the intersection of education, culture, and electoral participation in Northern Indigenous communities.

title: Understanding Economic Voting in Canadian Elections
description: Dr. Cameron Anderson, Professor of Political Science at Western University, presents his research on economic voting behaviour in Canadian federal elections.

title: GLOCAL Virtual Events
description: All of GLOCAL's upcoming and past events in one place, including regional showcases, virtual panels, and infographic poster series aimed at promoting civic engagement and electoral participation across Canada.

title: Disconnected and Distrustful: Analysis of Youth Mental Health, Political Trust, and Voter Participation in Canada
description: A comprehensive analysis of youth mental health trends in Canada and their correlation with political trust and voter participation, utilizing data from national surveys and electoral studies.

title: Youth Data Explorer
description: A website that allows users to explore various datasets from the Canada Elections Study related to youth political engagement, mental health, and voting behavior through interactive visualizations and dashboards.

title: Canadian Housing Data Hub
description: An interactive platform that consolidates and visualizes housing market data across Canada, providing insights into affordability, availability, and regional trends to inform policy-making and public understanding.

title: Canada's Housing Affordability Crisis: Analyzing Trends and Impacts
description: A comprehensive analysis of housing affordability trends in Canada, examining factors such as income levels, housing prices, and demographic shifts to understand the challenges faced by Canadians in accessing affordable housing.

title: Post-Covid E-Commerce Trends in Canada
description: How has e-commerce in Canada evolved since the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic? This project analyzes shifts in consumer behavior, market growth, and regional variations in online shopping across Canada.

title: Canadian Political Parties Database
description: Lillian Pianosi, Elias Titian, Joey Lee, Ethan Gallipeau, and Tim Guan compiled a national dataset of 358 Canadian political parties (340 active) over five weeks using Python/Pandas, addressing data quality challenges and identifying opportunities for automation and improved workflow design.

title: Debt Burden of Young Canadians: A Data-Driven Analysis
description: An in-depth analysis of the debt burden faced by young Canadians, exploring factors such as student loans, credit card debt, and housing costs, and their implications for financial stability and future economic prospects.

title: Awesome GLOCAL: Open Source Scripts
description: A curated list of useful, accessible scripts built by members of the GLOCAL community. Focused on simplifying workflows, improving usability, and supporting users across different technical skill levels.

title: Understanding Refugees in Canada
description: An accessible overview of Canada's refugee system, tracing the journey from initial application and eligibility determination through to arrival, integration, and long-term settlement — with a focus on the policies and supports that shape each stage.

title: Ontario Housing Affordability Dashboard
description: An interactive dashboard visualizing rental affordability trends across Ontario cities, comparing rent and income data to surface regional cost pressures and housing accessibility gaps.

title: From Pipes to People: Addressing Lead in Drinking Water
description: A health-based action toolkit for stakeholders and the public on lead contamination in drinking water, covering risks, prevention strategies, and practical resources for families and decision-makers.

title: Mental Health and Disability
description: A research-driven project translating mental health and disability policy insights into accessible public tools — including infographics, interactive quizzes, and a resource website — to bridge the gap between academic findings and everyday understanding.

title: Immigration Laws & Tips
description: An International Law 3201 project that identified gaps in how international students access legal protections in Canada, addressing them through simplified, actionable resources covering immigration, labour, safety, and human rights.

title: From Pandemic to Paycheque: How COVID-19 Changed Canadian Gen Z's First Job Age, Financial Literacy and Investment Habits
description: COVID-19 reduced youth employment and delayed early work experience for Gen Z, while economic pressures and increased digital engagement shaped their financial behaviour and learning.

title: Youcount Mobile App: Redesigning Access to Opportunity
description: A project by Sooa Lee, Jaden Seaforth, and Areeb Mohsin that identified usability issues in the YouCount platform and developed a mobile solution with simplified navigation, clearer terminology, and centralized user features.
embed: content/YouCount Mobile Design Project Group Presentation.pdf

title: Growing Plants in Our Arctic Classroom
description: At Inuksuk High School in Iqaluit, this initiative empowers students to grow their own vegetables and herbs indoors, a step toward reclaiming food resilience in one of the most expensive food regions in the country.

title: The Global Impact Fellowship
description: BacharLorai offers an 8-month online program for 10 youth (ages 18–25) to develop social impact leadership through workshops, networking, and a global capstone project supporting Bangladeshi diaspora communities in Canada, with public sharing of their learning and skills in areas like project management and advocacy.

title: Art Speaks: Integration Program
description: The project provides marginalized communities with safe spaces for artistic expression, storytelling, and peer support, promoting emotional awareness and a sense of belonging in an inclusive environment.

title: Preventing Gender-Based Violence in Canada
description: This project aims to inform and deepen understanding of gender-based violence (GBV) prevention in Canada by exploring its context, political and legal aspects, and the disproportionate impact on Indigenous communities, while empowering readers to engage in civic action to address GBV. Presented as a user-friendly website, the project supports CANConnect and GLOCAL Foundation's goals of civic engagement and knowledge mobilization.

title: Politics, Law, and the Challenge of Social Media Misinformation
description: The spread of misinformation on social media presents a serious threat to the security of democracies around the world. This project addresses the challenges of social media misinformation for Canadian policymaking by examining legal constraints to misinformation legislation in five comparable democracies: Germany, France, the U.K., the U.S., and Australia. The results of this comparative analysis help to advance a potential Canadian response to the problem of misinformation on social media with respect to Canada's unique legal and political context. The significance of this project is to enhance the public's understanding why responding to the problem of social media misinformation is so complicated and nuanced because responses must balance contradicting goals of protecting free speech and preventing harmful misinformation from spreading. However, as I demonstrate with this project, policymakers do not need to choose between one or other other. They can and have found ways to satisfy both.

title: How Air Quality is Important
description: The "How Air Quality is Important" project is dedicated to tackling pressing issues related to air quality with a multifaceted approach. By assessing and monitoring air quality levels, the project aims to educate local communities about the impact of pollution on health, ecosystems, and overall well-being. This initiative aligns seamlessly with the goals of civic engagement and civic knowledge mobilization set forth by the GLOCAL Foundation. Through the project, the emphasis is not only on fostering environmental awareness but also on empowering citizens with accessible information, engaging them in the democratic process, and providing opportunities for digital skill development. By addressing a global issue at the local level, the project contributes to a more inclusive, transparent, and engaging democratic participation, fostering a sense of global understanding among volunteers.

title: The Effects of Acid Rain
description: "The Effects of Acid Rain" project is a vital initiative focused on comprehensively investigating and understanding the repercussions of acid rain on ecosystems, human health, and infrastructure. By delving into the far-reaching impacts of acid rain, the project aims to contribute valuable insights that can inform international cooperation and policies aimed at mitigating its effects. The project aligns seamlessly with the goals of civic engagement and civic knowledge mobilization advocated by the GLOCAL Foundation. Ultimately, "The Effects of Acid Rain" project plays a crucial role in promoting a global understanding of environmental challenges and encouraging active participation in creating a sustainable and democratic future.

title: How to Cope with Social Anxiety Disorder
description: The "How to Cope with Social Anxiety Disorder" project provides crucial resources and coping strategies to help individuals manage social anxiety, aiming to enhance well-being and foster inclusivity. By promoting mental health awareness and support, it contributes to a more accessible and understanding society, aligning with the GLOCAL Foundation's values.

title: The Worst Day Ever? (a short film by Zoe Fraser)
description: The Worst Day Ever? is a short film about four siblings grappling with their mother’s decision to end her life through doctor-assisted death after a battle with cancer, exploring the controversial and newly legalized practice of MAiD in Canada and aiming to spark conversation about grief and societal views on death. The film seeks to reduce discomfort around discussing mortality, suggesting that sometimes facing the worst can ultimately be for the best.

title: web design: Internet Navigation Guide for Newcomers in Canada
description: Our project will develop a website that makes accurate civic information accessible and combats information overload by providing reliable, timely resources and guides, aligning with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation’s missions to promote digital civic engagement and informed citizenship. By leveraging technology, we aim to empower individuals and foster a more engaged, informed community.

title: Uncovering Our Unique Challenges: Case Studies Into Filipino and Ukrainian Immigrant Underreported and Unique Challenges Through Consulting With Canadian Ethnocultural Organizations
description: These Canva presentations provide overviews of Jollibee's history, competitive advantages in the fast-food industry, and strategic recommendations for future growth and global expansion.

title: Housifit - A House renting app.
description: Housifit is a mobile application designed to address Canada’s escalating housing demand—especially for immigrants and young Canadians—by streamlining tenant-landlord communication, enhancing property searches with creative, user-friendly features, and fostering community engagement. This innovative platform not only improves cost-efficiency and housing accessibility but also aligns with civic and community-focused goals advocated by CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation.

title: Newcomer's Guide: Unveiling Canada's Residential School History
description: I created a concise, accessible brochure using a Q&A format and impactful images to help newcomers in Canada better understand residential schools and the responsibilities of reconciliation, addressing widespread misinformation and fostering greater awareness of Indigenous issues. This initiative supports GLOCAL’s goal to build inclusive communities and reduce prejudice among immigrants and refugees by promoting accurate information and understanding about Indigenous peoples and their history.

title: Harmony in Law: Integrating Indigenous Legal Traditions
description: My project seeks to raise youth awareness about historical violations of Indigenous Peoples' rights by European settlers and highlight Indigenous beliefs that can benefit modern society, aiming to reduce prejudice and misinformation while promoting the value of traditional Indigenous knowledge in line with GLOCAL’s mission of fostering inclusive and socially innovative communities.

title: Hope Across The Border
description: A short documentary by Jilina Weng that journeys through the lives of Afghan refugees in Ottawa—from restaurant owner Fazil's culinary endeavors and musician Mushfiq's passion for Eastern classical music, to calligrapher Fahim's therapeutic art. The film also explores the Afghan Canadian Support Network and features conversations with Safia and Professor Sadat, weaving together powerful stories of resilience, cultural preservation, social integration, and community support.

title: Mandatory Hybrid Learning Option in Secondary Schools
description: Our project explores hybrid learning, a flexible educational model where students can attend classes either in person or virtually, which has grown during the COVID-19 pandemic. Implementing hybrid learning in secondary institutions would enhance student choice, reduce financial and commute burdens, and increase overall flexibility.

title: A Backwards Ocean
description: I created an oil painting titled "A Backwards Ocean" to highlight the contrast between healthy marine environments and the devastating effects of pollution, aiming to inspire civic engagement through ocean clean-up initiatives. Additionally, I provided information on accessible volunteer opportunities and included a brief policy analysis of Canada's ocean conservation efforts.

title: Financiable
description: Financiable, founded by students who experienced financial illiteracy, aims to make financial education more accessible for youth through online content and in-person seminars, helping them become confident, financially savvy adults. The initiative aligns with civic engagement goals and seeks to expand its impact, particularly among minority groups, recognizing that financial knowledge fosters positive change and equality.

title: Sustainable Business Showcase
description: As youths, we often lack the confidence, knowledge, and inspiration to start sustainable small businesses, which is why UNSD Youth organized an event to showcase Vancouver’s small business market and educate about sustainable practices, aiming to encourage community support and align with the goals of CANConnect and the Glocal Foundation.

title: Reducing Renters’ Carbon Footprint in the City of Vancouver
description: This research project examines the causes and challenges of renters’ carbon footprints in Vancouver, reviews academic literature and policy responses from other jurisdictions, and proposes equitable policy solutions to reduce rental sector emissions. The project was recognized with First Place at the Vancouver HUBBUB CityStudio Conference and was completed as part of UBC’s Graduate Program in Political Science.

title: Canada's Media Monitor
description: This project is a comprehensive system designed to collect and analyze a wide array of local public news and social media posts. Its primary aim is to convert large volumes of raw news data into usable and meaningful analytics. This project is driven by the necessity to interpret and quantify the changing stories and opinions found in our vast online media landscape, a task that is increasingly important for understanding political events and social trends that influence public conversations and policy-making.

title: Canada and the World: A Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats (SWOT) Analysis
description: This paper analyzes Canada’s position in a shifting global order through a SWOT analysis, arguing that the potential decline of the rules-based international order—due to the rise of China and the Indo-Pacific region—poses significant challenges for Canada’s international influence and economic wellbeing, making it a central concern for Canadian foreign policy. Understanding these dynamics is crucial for grasping the future of Canadian politics and their global implications.

title: Federalism Dynamics: Enhancing Policy Efficacy through Development, Administration, and Delivery Strategies
description: This project critically analyzes the role of Federalism in shaping public policy development, administration, and delivery in Canada, using the healthcare system as a case study to illustrate both its advantages and drawbacks. By bridging civic engagement and knowledge mobilization, it provides insights and recommendations to inform policymakers and empower citizens in governance discussions, aligning with the objectives of CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation.

title: Analysis of food waste in Canadian agriculture
description: In Canada, farm-level food loss costs about CAD 2.88 billion annually—22% of national food waste—while food insecurity affects 16% of Canadians, yet the issue remains largely unaddressed. This youth-led project aims to minimize agricultural food waste, support sustainable farming, and combat food insecurity through awareness, advocacy, and civic engagement, in partnership with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation.

title: Chairing G20 Summits: Global Governance and Cooperation in a Changing World Order
description: This project highlights Canada's pivotal role in promoting inclusion, democracy, and rule of law amidst rising global risks and shifting power dynamics, advocating for strategic diplomacy to foster resilient and peaceful global governance. Canada should avoid escalating tensions with China, leverage its positive international image, and help transition towards a more multipolar and cooperative world order.

title: Canadian in Bangla Town
description: The 'Canadian in Bangla Town' photobook captures the cultural, social, and historical narratives of Toronto’s Bangladeshi diaspora, aiming to address their underrepresentation through vivid storytelling and visual documentation. The project fosters civic engagement, cultural appreciation, and societal connection while serving as a platform for education, dialogue, and community building.

title: Young and Black
description: Racial discrimination in Canadian workplaces significantly contributes to mental health challenges among young Black professionals, leading to issues like anxiety, depression, and substance abuse, with over half reporting workplace discrimination as a major cause. This not only affects individual well-being but also impacts organizational productivity and the wider economy.

title: HomeHarmony: Unveiling the Canadian Real Estate Tapestry
description: HomeHarmony aims to provide stakeholders with insightful, visually engaging representations of Canada’s real estate landscape by harmonizing diverse housing data through various visualizations. The project leverages multiple datasets and visualization techniques to deliver a comprehensive, nuanced understanding of market trends, dwelling types, and regional dynamics.

title: Data-Driven Dreams: Empowering International Students' Career Choices
description: Data Driven Dreams is an interactive dashboard that helps over 400,000 international students in Ontario navigate postsecondary education and make informed career choices by providing personalized insights based on their chosen university program. This project, created by community leaders and supported by Engage, aims to empower students and transform their educational journey into a tool for personal and professional growth.

title: Plastic Pollution and the Marine Environment: Current and Future Challenges
description: The objective of my research project is to raise awareness about plastic marine pollution and its impacts, promote sustainable waste solutions, and increase civic engagement through partnerships between local residents, CANConnect, and the GLOCAL Foundation. By mobilizing knowledge and fostering community involvement, the project aims to empower individuals to take action and change behaviors to reduce plastic waste in the oceans.

title: Housing Affordability in Canadian Politics Informational Website
description: This project aims to clarify the complex factors driving rising home prices in Canada’s housing market—especially in cities like Vancouver and Toronto—by providing accessible information, analyzing political influences, and proposing solutions to empower diverse groups such as new immigrants, students, and aspiring homeowners. Through knowledge mobilization and educational resources, the project seeks to foster civic dialogue, enhance understanding, and encourage informed participation in addressing Canadian housing affordability.

title: Pierre Trudeau’s Legacy: An Analysis of Policy Judgements and Contributions to Separatism
description: My project examines Pierre Trudeau's influence on separatism in Canada through his policies, particularly regarding bilingualism, by exploring how these decisions shaped language and cultural divides, and assessing their relevance and effectiveness in regions like metro Vancouver where French is rarely spoken.

title: The Impact of Climate Change on Quebec's Tourism Industry
description: This project examines the impact of climate change on Quebec's tourism industry as a case study to highlight broader climate-related challenges, aiming to raise awareness and spur innovative, collective solutions. By mobilizing knowledge and engaging diverse stakeholders, the project seeks to foster civic engagement, inform policy, and contribute to sustainable development and resilience in tourism and beyond.

title: Understanding Credit Score and Its Importance In Canada
description: A credit score is a three-digit number, typically ranging from 300 to 850, that reflects your creditworthiness based on your credit history and is used by lenders to determine your eligibility and terms for credit. It significantly impacts your financial opportunities and access to loans.

title: How Citizens are influenced by Political Party Candidates
description: This project investigates how citizens' voting habits are influenced not only by party values and commitments but also by the personal characteristics of political party candidates—such as age, gender, and ethnicity—highlighting the role of civic engagement and knowledge mobilization in shaping electoral support.

title: Navigating Waste: A Comprehensive Analysis of Waste Management Practices in Canada, The United States, China and Australia.
description: This study examines waste management practices in Canada, the United States, China, and Australia, with a detailed focus on Canadian landfill trends, governance, and 2002–2020 data. In Canada, waste per person has declined despite total waste rising, likely due to increased public awareness and improved recycling efforts, reflecting effective multi-level waste governance.

title: How to Succeed in Canada as a newly arrived refugee; by education and work.
description: This project guides newly arrived refugees in Canada on how to quickly integrate into society and the workforce by focusing on learning English, navigating the education system, exploring career options, gaining relevant work experience, and understanding Canadian culture. It aims to support refugees in continuing their education and achieving professional success in Canada.

title: Newcomers and Financial Literacy
description: Newcomers and Financial Literacy empowers immigrants by addressing the specific financial challenges they face—such as understanding banking, managing credit, and adapting to new financial systems—to promote their economic integration and self-sufficiency. This project aligns with the goals of CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation by advancing information mobilization, civic engagement, and community cohesion through financial literacy education for newcomers.

title: Baqir Ahmadi an immigrant Life journey to Canada
description: Baqir Ahmadi is an immigrant whose journey to Canada serves to inspire others not to give up on their goals. His story encourages perseverance and determination in pursuing one’s dreams.

title: Understanding Moroccan Communities in Canada
description: The project seeks to explore the diverse challenges Moroccan Canadians face following the recent earthquake in Morocco, focusing on humanitarian aid, mental health, employment issues, and the preservation of cultural heritage. Its goal is to better understand and address these post-earthquake needs within the community.

title: Understanding the Journey: Afghan Refugees in Canada Briefly (2021-2022)
description: The project aims to document and share the experiences of Afghan refugees who arrived in Canada in 2021/2022, highlighting their challenges and raising awareness to foster greater understanding and empathy within the wider community.

title: Local youth empowerment center
description: My narrative-based project, titled 'Local Youth Community Center,' will feature well-structured paragraphs, engaging images, and instructive videos to effectively support and enhance the content.

title: Canadian Culture and Newcomer Culture.  Similarities and Contrasts
description: This project explores the similarities and differences between Canadian culture and the cultures of newcomers, highlighting how they interact, influence each other, and coexist within Canada. It aims to provide a better understanding of cultural integration and diversity in Canadian society.

title: A Guide to Canadian Copyright Law: A Young Canadian's Best Friend in Navigating Fair Dealing Online
description: This project explores copyright, piracy, and academic integrity to help youth understand their legal rights and responsibilities, making complex legal concepts accessible and relevant to their academic and personal lives. By breaking down these ideas, the project aims to empower students to respect others’ work and prepare them for future educational and professional challenges.

title: The Story Of An Afghan Diplomat’s Daughter
description: You described how you and your family went through many challenges, but also experienced positive moments along the way.

title: Helping Newcomers To Navigate the System
description: The project aims to support newcomers by developing an online platform that provides accessible information and resources on essential services, local governance, and cultural integration, addressing the challenges they face in navigating unfamiliar systems. Through this centralized resource hub, the initiative seeks to empower newcomers and promote seamless community integration.

title: Notes of the North Podcast: A Celebration of Canadian Composers
description: Notes of the North is a podcast and website that highlights lesser-known Canadian composers and their music, celebrating the country’s multicultural diversity and fostering civic and global engagement through accessible stories and episodes. With the help of a microgrant, the project plans to spotlight 60 composers in 2024, broaden its cultural inclusivity, and expand its reach through major streaming platforms.

title: The mental health of Indigenous children in Residential Schools in Canada and what Canadian Social workers did for this Situation.
description: Indigenous children in Canadian Residential Schools suffered significant mental health trauma due to cultural assimilation, abuse, and separation from family, while for decades, most Canadian social workers largely supported the system or remained complicit, only beginning to advocate for Indigenous children's rights and healing in more recent years.

title: How to Write a Resume
description: This project assists new immigrants in Canada by teaching them how to write effective resumes, helping them improve their job prospects and achieve employment success.

title: THE CANADIAN PARLIAMENT And its impacts on laws and policies
description: The Canadian Parliament is the federal legislative body responsible for creating, amending, and repealing laws, significantly shaping national policies and governance. Its decisions impact Canadians’ rights, social programs, and the country’s direction on domestic and international issues.

title: Single Mother
description: Single motherhood, increasingly common today, involves both significant challenges—like financial hardship and societal stigma—and meaningful rewards, such as strong parent-child bonds and positive role modeling, highlighting the need for supportive communities to help single mothers thrive.

title: Analysis of Public Utilities Development in Canada
description: This project seeks to enhance community economic resilience by developing a framework that links employment opportunities with affordable pricing of essential goods, fostering stability and well-being. It aligns with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation by promoting civic engagement, knowledge mobilization, and sustainable, inclusive economic practices at the local level.

title: REQUEST FOR GENDER-NEUTRAL MENSTRUAL PRODUCTS TO BE AVAILABLE FREE IN ALL BATHROOM STALLS IN CANADA
description: Providing menstrual products in all bathrooms is crucial to addressing period poverty and advancing menstrual equity, as it challenges systemic sexism and the male-default bias perpetuated by patriarchy. This project aims to create a more inclusive and equitable environment for all.

title: Unhoused Refugees in Ontario
description: This project examines the housing support available to Government Assisted Refugees and Refugee Claimants/Asylum Seekers, identifies barriers to housing, and highlights the significance of addressing these challenges. It aims to raise awareness through infographics and possibly interviews, making resources and refugee voices accessible to a wider audience.

title: Welcome to Your New “Home”: Acculturation in First- and Second-Generation Immigrants
description: My research examines how family dynamics and identity factors shape acculturation patterns—assimilation, separation, integration, and marginalization—among first- and second-generation immigrants in Canada, aiming to identify barriers and facilitators of successful adaptation. The findings will inform evidence-based policies and interventions that support immigrant well-being, promote civic engagement, and foster inclusive communities in line with the goals of CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation.

title: Champions of Inclusion: Youth Leaders Camp
description: The Youth Leadership Camp empowers 20 high school students to establish "inclusion clubs" that promote belonging and support for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, providing them with resources and training to raise awareness and foster inclusive communities. The student who secures the most pledges for inclusion will be recognized as “Youth Leader of the Year” at a virtual event, highlighting the impact of youth-driven social change.

title: Documenting First Aid Traditions in Indigenous Communities and Low-Resource Communities across Nova Scotia: A Cultural Anthropology Perspective
description: EmergAid addresses the lack of emergency preparedness in low-resourced communities by developing and distributing a culturally relevant Improvised First Aid Manual, alongside community workshops. Collaborating with healthcare professionals, indigenous leaders, and artists, the project empowers individuals to respond to emergencies and fosters civic engagement and inclusivity.

title: Beaver Quiz-A-Mole
description: This interactive, arcade-style game challenges players to answer questions about Canada by tapping beavers with the correct answers in a vibrant, fast-paced “whack-a-mole” format, offering both single and multi-player modes, educational tidbits, adjustable difficulty, and scoring features designed to make learning Canadian civic knowledge fun and engaging for youth.

title: The Youth Outreach Program
description: We founded a nonprofit to give all youth, regardless of background or prior experience, accessible leadership opportunities and a supportive community, removing barriers often found in traditional student councils. Through events like game nights, a Model UN conference, and member-led initiatives, we've empowered over 15 new members to create positive change and grow as leaders in their communities.

title: Assessment: Settlement Journey of Afghan Newcomers in Calgary, Alberta
description: This study explores the complex settlement and integration challenges faced by Afghan newcomers and recent citizens in Calgary, providing refugee-supporting organizations with valuable insights to guide policies and programs. Using both on-site and desk review data collection methods, the survey achieved a 94% participation rate, lending credibility to its findings.

title: Homelessness in Canada
description: The lack of a proper resource made the process time-consuming and required extra effort despite the abundance of available materials.

title: EmpowerBlack Youth Entrepreneurship Pitch Competition
description: This initiative aims to empower black youth entrepreneurs by hosting an in-person networking summit featuring business leaders, a pop-up shop, and a pitch competition, providing opportunities to showcase their ideas, connect with peers, and receive support and recognition for their ventures.

title: Rise and Shine Series
description: The "Rise and Shine Series" is an interview project aimed at amplifying Ethiopian and Eritrean youth voices by sharing diverse personal stories, celebrating cultural heritage, and challenging stereotypes to inspire civic engagement and community building. Through interviews with individuals from varied backgrounds, the series seeks to foster understanding, raise awareness, and empower young people to actively participate in their communities.

title: English Language Learning for Systems Navigation and Civic Engagement
description: Our proposed two-month “English Language Learning for Systems Navigation and Civic Engagement” program aims to help refugee parents overcome language and civic knowledge barriers so they can advocate for their children and participate more fully in Canadian schools and communities. By building practical English skills and providing essential information on local education systems and civic processes, the program will support both parents’ and children’s integration and development.

title: Analysis on international students in Ontario
description: This Power BI project analyzes Ontario's post-secondary enrollment trends from 2012 to 2024 by gender, age, program, and mother tongue, providing data-driven insights to inform policies, optimize resources, and promote inclusivity. By making this information accessible, the project encourages civic engagement, community awareness, and dialogue to enhance Ontario's educational landscape.

title: Combating Barriers to Mental Health among Racialized Immigrants in Canada: An Analysis of Factors Affecting Access to Mental Health Services
description: This project aims to investigate the risk factors and barriers affecting access to mental health services among racialized immigrants in Canada, with the goal of using research findings to develop a web-based resource that increases awareness and supports the mental well-being of this population.

title: Educational Centre for Indigenous Environmental Justice
description: My research project is a website that educates users about how climate change disproportionately affects Indigenous Peoples in Canada, aiming to bridge the gap between academic research and public knowledge while motivating readers to take civic action through resources like a “Take Action” section. The project highlights the intersectionality of climate change and calls for advocacy for Indigenous rights and autonomy on their unceded territories.

title: Journey to Maple Dreams
description: Journey to Maple Dreams follows Nancy Diop, an 18-year-old from Senegal pursuing environmental science in Canada, highlighting the challenges of accessing education abroad and emphasizing unequal opportunities. The project seeks to foster empathy, promote dialogue on global education issues, and support CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation's mission of civic engagement and positive social change.

title: Menstrual Hygiene Management: Exploring the Unspoken
description: The project aims to empower Bangladeshi international female students in Toronto by co-creating culturally relevant menstrual health management (MHM) programs, fostering leadership, and dispelling period-related myths and stigma. By creating supportive spaces for MHM discussions and aligning with UN Sustainable Development Goals, the initiative seeks to improve educational outcomes, social participation, and gender equity within both local and global contexts.

title: YouthSpeak Social Media Influencer Project
description: YouthSpeak conducts school assemblies addressing mental health and youth empowerment, observing recurring student concerns such as homophobia, sexism, racism, and unhealthy choices, often influenced by social media. Through research, the project aims to better understand these issues, enhance presentations, and empower students to build more inclusive, resilient communities.

title: Food Security in Waterloo Region: A Volunteer's Perspective
description: This research examines the interconnected issues of food insecurity and homelessness in Waterloo Region through direct collaboration with community organizations, highlighting their roles in providing essential services. It offers recommendations for enhanced collaboration, innovation, and community engagement to address root causes and build a more inclusive, sustainable society.

title: Pelee Island Legion Senior Socials
description: The Royal Canadian Legion Branch 403 serves as the essential community hub for Pelee Island’s small, mostly senior population, providing a vital space for connection and support, particularly during the isolating winter months when the island is accessible only by plane. However, due to declining resources and the pandemic, many regular events have ceased, heightening seniors' need for more opportunities to engage and combat isolation.

title: History of the Liberal Party
description: This research paper explores the history of the Liberal Party and its leaders, aiming to offer newcomers and those interested in Canadian political history a clear and reliable overview of the party’s development.

title: The Role of Civic Engagement in Addressing the Civic Issues of South Sudanese Youth in Canada
description: This project investigates how distrust in law enforcement, youth disengagement from democratic processes, and levels of civic participation affect the civic life, identity, and social outcomes—such as crime and homelessness—among South Sudanese youth in Calgary. The research aligns with CANConnect and GLOCAL Foundation’s missions by empowering youth, fostering civic awareness, and promoting inclusivity within the community.

title: Global governance on Campus - Creating a Global Impact
description: Our project seeks to empower youth and enhance civic involvement in Canada by raising awareness about the impact of humanitarian aid and encouraging informed, socially conscious participation, while promoting sustainability and aligning with the values of CANConnect and GLOCAL. We believe that by educating and engaging young people, we can foster meaningful global change and social progress.

title: Youth Digital Talent Empowerment Program
description: Youth Digital Talent empowers immigrant and refugee youth aged 14-24 by providing digital skills training and paid, project-based work creating digital solutions for nonprofits and small businesses, helping bridge the digital divide while fostering civic engagement and leadership. This initiative offers equitable access to learning and work opportunities, alleviating financial burdens and supporting community contributions in alignment with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation’s goals.

title: Refugees in Canada
description: This research explores the experiences and struggles of refugees in Canada, highlighting both the challenges they face and the support they receive, with the goal of fostering greater understanding and respect among Canadian youth. It aims to promote civic knowledge and engagement by sharing refugee stories and encouraging Canadians to consider and address refugee issues.

title: CHILD WELFARE AND INDIGENOUS CHILDREN
description: My project, "CHILD WELFARE AND INDIGENOUS CHILDREN," focuses on the historical and ongoing challenges faced by indigenous children, including government policies that removed them from their families, forced assimilation in Christian schools, suppression of their languages, and exposure to abuse from teachers.

title: Humans in Flight
description: Humans in Flight is a project that amplifies refugee voices in Canada to challenge stereotypes, celebrate their contributions, and foster empathy through visual storytelling and community engagement. By promoting inclusivity and multiculturalism, it aims to build understanding and social cohesion, aligning with broader civic engagement goals.

title: Autistic Masking: motivations, strategies and consequences
description: Autistic masking challenges the theory of mind deficits by demonstrating that autistic individuals are aware of how they are perceived and intentionally suppress or alter behaviors to fit in socially, using strategies like instinctive and active masking to minimize victimization. However, this camouflaging can lead to serious mental health consequences, including increased anxiety from fear of judgment and depression from prolonged inauthenticity.

title: Harmony in Diversity: Unraveling the Tapestry of Same-Sex Marriage Perspectives in Canada
description: This project analyzes how education and various social factors influence attitudes toward same-sex marriage in Canada using advanced statistical methods and the 2015 Canadian Election Study, offering actionable insights for policymakers and organizations like CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation to promote civic engagement and informed dialogue on social issues. The research not only advances academic understanding but also supports knowledge mobilization and fosters positive societal change through a nuanced exploration of public opinion.

title: CliniScan: Mapping Healthcare Availability in Canada
description: This project maps the provincial distribution of healthcare facilities, offering insights to help decision-makers plan and improve public health services.

title: Our London Lights' Kits
description: The project provides "Our London Lights' Kits"—containing handmade games, crafts, and positive messages—to uplift and support young patients at the Children's Hospital at London Health Sciences Centre, offering comfort and engagement during extended stays. This initiative also advances civic engagement and knowledge mobilization by involving the community, raising awareness of children's healthcare challenges, and fostering empathy.

title: Relations in Canada
description: This project examines the structure and effectiveness of intergovernmental relations, ministries, and programs in Canada—particularly the Canada-Wide program—while highlighting how their organization often excludes certain groups, especially Indigenous peoples, from decision-making processes, thereby undermining regional representation and civic engagement.

title: New Young immigrants in Canada
description: My research project aims to improve the integration and well-being of young new immigrants in Canada by identifying their unique challenges, analyzing factors for successful integration, evaluating existing support programs, and proposing evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: Single Parenting / Single Mothers
description: Single mothers often face financial struggles and societal stigma, but they also build strong bonds with their children and exemplify resilience; understanding their unique experiences highlights the importance of community support and encouragement for this family type.

title: Shakiba A Persian girl's name meaning one who is Patient/Tolerative.
description: I am writing and illustrating a book about Shakeba, an Afghan girl whose refugee journey to Canada highlights both the challenges and triumphs of starting over, anxiously awaiting reunion with her mother, and ultimately finding resilience through a positive attitude. The story aims to deepen understanding among immigrant and non-immigrant readers alike about the privileges of life in Canada while authentically portraying the refugee experience.

title: The Global Impact Fellowship
description: BacharLorai's 8-month online program empowers 10 youth aged 18–25 to become social impact leaders through skills workshops, networking, and a global capstone project supporting Bangladeshi diaspora communities in Canada. Fellows share their learning online to benefit a broader audience.

title: A Comparative Study of Health and Fitness in Canada and Afghanistan
description: The project analyzed health and fitness practices in Canada and Afghanistan, exploring how cultural, economic, and societal factors shape physical well-being. By collaborating with experts and communities, it identified key differences in policies, access, and habits to encourage healthier lifestyles.

title: Youth Innovating for Change
description: This documentary showcases how young leaders harness digital platforms to address issues such as inequality, food insecurity, mental health, and homelessness. By highlighting youth-led initiatives and exploring the root causes of these challenges, it educates and empowers viewers to use digital tools for civic engagement and drive a more equitable future.

title: Digital Inclusion Webcasts for Seniors
description: The Digital Inclusion Webcasts for Seniors project offered online sessions and resources to help older adults develop digital skills and foster inclusion. Through partnerships with community organizations, it empowered seniors to overcome digital barriers and participate more actively in society.

title: Youth-Led Civic Engagement Initiatives
description: The Incubator for Youth-Led Civic Engagement Initiatives empowers the Youth Senators Parliamentary Group (YSPG) to advocate for youth-focused policies and strengthen civic engagement among young Canadians. It serves as a platform for youth-led initiatives in policy analysis, community engagement, and outreach, addressing issues like mental health, housing affordability, and political participation.

title: New Beginnings: The Afghan Experience in Fredericton
description: The documentary explores the experiences, challenges, and contributions of Afghan newcomers as they integrate into the Fredericton community. It sheds light on their journeys and the impact they have on local society.

title: Inclusive Leadership Web Seminar Series
description: The Inclusive Leadership Web Seminar Series is a two-part live seminar initiative aimed at promoting inclusive leadership practices. The project will equip professionals and leaders with actionable strategies to foster diversity, equity, and inclusion in their organizations. Participants will gain tools and insights to create inclusive workplaces, enhancing team performance and fostering a culture of belonging.

title: Nritya for Community
description: The Natya Collective, in collaboration with the South Asian Women's Community Centre in Montreal, provides free dance classes to South Asian immigrant women and their families, promoting community, cultural connection, and accessibility, while also giving local dancers opportunities to teach and share their passion.

title: SkySight Fort Resolution: Capturing Community Perspectives
description: This project uses drone technology in Fort Resolution to capture and preserve community history, culture, and events while giving students hands-on experience in STEM, photography, and digital storytelling. Through training, community projects, and sharing content, it promotes education, engagement, and collaboration, helping students and residents document and celebrate their community.

title: Visionary Voices: Youth Empowerment through Civic Engagement Video Series
description: The Youth Empowerment through Civic Engagement Video Series empowers marginalized youth in Ottawa by equipping them with technical skills to create videos on social issues like gun violence and substance abuse, while offering them a platform to share their perspectives and highlight the value of civic engagement.

title: Reclaiming Reading Website
description: The Reclaiming Reading Website is an online resource that supports youth in learning to read their native languages through educational tools and collaborative book creation, aiming to preserve language and culture while reducing cultural alienation among Canadian immigrant communities.

title: STEM Mentorship Podcast for Youth
description: The STEM Mentorship Podcast for Youth is a two-day virtual event where STEM professionals share personal stories and advice to inspire and guide young people toward STEM careers, fostering mentorship, awareness, and community support.

title: Securikey: Improving Safety for Youth in Canada
description: Securikey enhances the mental and physical well-being of Canadian youth by digitizing specialized safety tips and resources on their website, empowering them to feel more confident and secure. This initiative is supported by GLOCAL’s CANConnect Diversity Micro-grant Program.

title: Universal Basic Income
description: A debate video on Universal Basic Income (UBI) educates viewers by presenting balanced perspectives from ordinary people, using visual aids to highlight both benefits and drawbacks, with the goal of increasing understanding and encouraging government consideration of UBI's viability.

title: Raising Awareness About Civic Engagement Opportunities for Canadian Youth
description: This Instagram account raises awareness about civic engagement opportunities for Canadian youth by sharing interviews, posts, and accessible resources. It serves as a central platform to educate and connect young people to opportunities through curated content and easy-to-access links.

title: Empowering Youth Voices Through Collaboration
description: The initiative unites youth leaders, civil society, and media figures in North America to enhance youth advocacy through strategic partnerships, stakeholder meetings, and media campaigns. It focuses on impactful engagement and effective management to drive social change.

title: Inclusive Canada
description: Inclusive Canada magazine leverages memes to amplify youth voices on inclusivity, sharing diverse experiences and sparking important conversations to empower young people in building a more equitable society.

title: An E-Learning Toolkit for Iranian Newcomers in Canada
description: The project offers customized educational resources, tools, and community support to help Iranian immigrants navigate immigration, overcome barriers, and integrate into Canadian society, while promoting inclusion, belonging, and civic engagement.

title: My Family Journey: From Afghanistan to Canada
description: My Family Journey: From Afghanistan to Canada tells the story of fleeing Afghanistan and resettling in Canada, and emphasizes the importance of kindness and community support for refugees through partnerships with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation.

title: A Daughter from Herat: The Journey of Marzia
description: A Daughter from Herat: The Journey of Marzia recounts Marzia's courageous struggle for freedom and women's rights in Afghanistan, showcasing her resilience as she overcomes adversity and rebuilds her life across borders.

title: Financial Literacy Curriculum
description: The project seeks to close the financial literacy gap among Ontario youth by introducing a customized, engaging school curriculum that equips students with vital money management skills, empowering them to make informed financial decisions for lifelong success.

title: Tote-ally Artsy
description: This project hosts a tote bag paint night around exam season that combines creative expression with mental health education for high school and university students. Through expert guidance, presentations on mental health in Canada, and community outreach, it aims to reduce stigma, promote awareness of available supports, and encourage healthier coping strategies.

title: Financial Literacy Program for Newcomers
description: The Financial Literacy Program helps newcomers in Canada build essential money management skills through workshops and online resources, enabling them to make informed financial decisions and better integrate into the Canadian economy.

title: Unlocking Your Potential: Youth Career Opportunities
description: The project supports immigrant girls in developing a growth mindset, setting career goals, and building confidence, while teaching job market awareness and organizational skills to foster financial independence, community engagement, and personal development. It aims to help them overcome challenges and reach their full potential.

title: Through the Continent
description: The "Through the Continent" podcast initiative connects African and Caribbean cultures by sharing diverse voices, stories, and insights, fostering cross-cultural understanding. It targets audiences interested in the rich histories, identities, and innovations of these regions through interviews, narratives, and analysis.

title: Online Safety for Educators Webcast Series
description: The Online Safety for Educators Webcast Series provides educators with key cybersecurity skills to protect their digital classrooms and personal data. Through four live sessions with expert guidance and interactive Q&As, it covers topics like password management, phishing awareness, and data protection.

title: Green Together
description: Green Together is a community project that helps marginalized groups grow their own food indoors using sustainable methods. Through workshops and starter kits, it promotes self-sufficiency, improves access to fresh food, and encourages healthier, environmentally conscious living.

title: JEDI Champions
description: JEDI Champions is a youth-led initiative that empowers underrepresented students with technical training, leadership skills, and mentorship to design civic solutions focused on justice, equity, decolonization, and inclusion. Through personalized support, it fosters systemic change and enhances civic engagement and knowledge mobilization.

title: The Youth Tutoring Project
description: The Youth Tutoring Project (YTP) provides free tutoring to underserved K-8 students in Ottawa, Toronto, Vancouver, and India, aiming to improve educational access and equity, especially for refugee and immigrant students affected by COVID-19-related disparities.

title: Green Connect
description: The project enables civilians to quickly locate nearby open spaces that regularly host activities.

title: Empowering Women Entrepreneurs Podcast Series
description: This platform supports women entrepreneurs by sharing diverse stories, offering practical resources, and building community connections, with a launch event featuring live interviews and pre-recorded episodes to promote empowerment, education, and collaboration. It aims to inspire women to support each other and take initiative in business.

title: Women’s Voices
description: Women’s Voices fosters civic engagement and social responsibility by providing a platform for open dialogue on issues impacting young women, amplifying diverse perspectives to inspire awareness, advocacy, and community participation. Its interviews create a sense of agency and inclusivity around topics like mental health, sexuality, and faith.

title: HYPE podcast
description: The HYPE podcast supports marginalized youth by offering mental health and financial literacy education, combating stigma, and encouraging open dialogue. Through mentorship and sharing real-life experiences, it fosters community and equips young people with confidence and practical skills.

title: Healthy Habits Live Weekend Workshop
description: A two-day virtual event offered expert-led education on nutrition, physical activity, and stress management, promoting sustainable lifestyle changes through interactive sessions and resources. It supported CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation’s mission to empower individuals and build resilient communities through personalized learning and engagement.

title: Young & Black Canada
description: The organization empowers young Black professionals through mental health and career development support, leveraging technology and social media to provide culturally relevant resources, while aligning with UN Goals 3 and 8 to educate, inspire, and advocate via its online platforms and podcast.

title: Rhythm and Roots
description: Rhythm & Roots is a youth-led program that empowers Afro-Indigenous and Caribbean girls in Regent Park through dance, promoting cultural expression and community engagement. Through workshops and events, it helps participants build confidence, teamwork skills, and a stronger connection to their heritage.

title: Through Our Lens – The Story of Fort Resolution
description: Students in Grades 10–12 from Fort Resolution, Northwest Territories, used photography to document and celebrate their community, and shared their stories nationally in Ottawa.

title: MarineMatch
description: MarineMatch is an Android app that uses a convolutional neural network to identify over 60 ocean species from photos, offering species information and conservation status to support responsible fishing and marine stewardship, especially for Indigenous and coastal communities.

title: EduInsight
description: EduInsight offers a digital control panel that delivers comprehensive, timely data on higher education performance indicators, enabling students to make informed educational and career decisions. This tool supports student success and long-term resilience by increasing transparency in higher education.

title: BeABLE
description: Our project examines how AI can support disabled Canadians, particularly those awaiting PWD applications, by enhancing access to resources through a website and research, while also analyzing civic engagement, current systems, and strategies for greater accessibility.

title: Ku Gicaniro
description: Ku Gicaniro is a community initiative that brings together young Rwandans in Canada to foster cultural awareness, social responsibility, and civic engagement through mentorship, storytelling, and cultural discussions. Inspired by the Rwandan tradition of gathering by the fire, it encourages youth to connect with their heritage and roles as engaged citizens.

title: Finovate Hacks
description: The Fintech Hackathon is an event designed for developers, entrepreneurs, and industry professionals to collaboratively develop innovative financial technology solutions, focusing on addressing real-world challenges like digital banking, financial inclusion, and blockchain applications. Its main goal is to offer a platform for showcasing creativity and technical expertise.

title: A Platform for Youth-Led Policy Innovation
description: The initiative establishes a sustainable framework for youth-led policy innovation by connecting youth leaders with international women’s rights activists across the U.S., promoting dialogue on gender equality, sharing advocacy strategies, and building enduring partnerships.

title: Empowering Marginalized Youth through Mental Wellness and Creative Expression
description: Live More Canada fosters safe, stigma-free spaces for mental health discussions, especially among Black and immigrant communities, using community support, creativity, and therapy to promote healing, cultural reconnection, and resilience.

title: The Judicial System: Examining the Role of Public Confidence and Enhancing Public Trust
description: The project seeks to rebuild public trust in the BC judicial system by developing an accessible online platform that centralizes reliable information, enhancing citizens' understanding and promoting democratic participation.

title: Digital Marketing for Small Businesses Webinar Series
description: The Digital Marketing for Small Businesses Webinar Series is a two-day Zoom event offering practical tools and strategies in SEO, content, and social media to help small business owners boost online visibility. The program features actionable guidance, checklists, and templates to promote growth and digital self-sufficiency for local entrepreneurs.

title: Empowering Voices: Insights into Advancing Autism Awareness and Legislation in Canada
description: The project reviews Canadian laws impacting individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder to identify and address shortcomings in accessibility, service quality, and awareness. Engaging stakeholders, it seeks to promote inclusive policy reform and align with the GLOCAL Foundation’s advocacy for understanding and equity.

title: Baked Blessings
description: Baked Blessings is a youth-led initiative that combats food insecurity by serving nutritious meals and teaching young volunteers vital life skills through community engagement. By collaborating with local partners, it empowers youth to lead with compassion and fosters lasting social responsibility.

title: Small Business Cybersecurity Webinar
description: Faraz Butt, a 24-year-old tech enthusiast, launched a webinar series to make cybersecurity accessible for small business owners, aiming to boost their confidence and digital safety.

title: Stories Without Borders
description: Stories Without Borders is a digital storytelling initiative in Canada that highlights refugee resilience and contributions through interviews and digital art, challenging victim narratives and promoting social inclusion and civic engagement in alignment with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation’s objectives.

title: Women in Tech Career Podcast Series
description: The Women in Tech Career Podcast Series is a two-day virtual event featuring real stories and advice from women in technology to inspire and empower aspiring women, particularly from underrepresented communities. It aims to address mentorship gaps, promote inclusive pathways, and support leadership development in the tech industry.

title: Constructing Affordable and Sustainable Housing using 3D printing Technology in Vancouver
description: This research explores how 3D printing can offer a more affordable, efficient, and sustainable solution to the housing crisis in Vancouver and across Canada. By testing a prototype 3D-printed house model, it demonstrates the technology’s potential to improve construction speed, reduce costs, and set new standards for sustainable urban housing.

title: A Place to Call Home
description: The project explores housing challenges for Afghan newcomers in Ottawa, Canada, focusing on financial aid, support organizations, and policies, with the goal of raising awareness, providing resources, and advocating for policy improvements to support their integration.

title: Language Preservation Webcasts
description: The Language Preservation Webcasts project is a live series designed to promote the revitalization and preservation of endangered languages. Featuring expert panels and interactive sessions, the webcasts will provide participants with practical strategies for safeguarding linguistic heritage. Participants will gain insights into language preservation techniques, cultural significance, and community-led efforts, with supplementary resources such as vocabulary guides and cultural materials provided to reinforce learning.

title: We Are Changemakers
description: We Are Changemakers is a documentary series highlighting immigrant and Afro-descendant entrepreneurs in Ottawa/Gatineau who run social enterprises addressing social issues, aiming to boost their visibility and representation. The project uses multimedia storytelling to promote inclusion, civic engagement, and connections that empower diverse entrepreneurs and drive social change.

title: Environmental Advocacy Webcasts
description: The Environmental Advocacy Webcasts project is a live monthly series designed to raise awareness about both local and global environmental challenges. The initiative will offer expert-led panel discussions, case studies, and interactive Q&A sessions to empower participants with actionable strategies for sustainable practices and environmental advocacy. By fostering real-time engagement and knowledge sharing, the project seeks to inspire individuals and communities to advocate for environmental preservation.

title: Volunteerism Through Interactive Webcasts
description: The Volunteerism Through Interactive Webcasts project aims to inspire community engagement by showcasing volunteer opportunities, success stories, and community impact. Through a series of live interactive webcasts, participants will connect with meaningful volunteer programs. The initiative features real-time discussions, expert-led presentations, and practical resources designed to promote a culture of service and action within local communities.

title: Financial Literacy Clinic
description: This project promotes financial literacy by providing community members with accessible tools and education to better understand and manage their finances. Through free tax assistance, workshops, and resources, it empowers individuals to make informed decisions and participate more confidently in their economic well-being.

title: Building Bridges for Global Youth Advocacy
description: The project seeks to empower youth in global advocacy by fostering dialogue between young leaders and policymakers, highlighted by a roundtable with Bob Rae and U.S. State Department representatives, to create strategies that elevate youth voices in decision-making.

title: Exploring Photovoice as an Impact Measurement Tool for Underfunded Youth-Led Organizing in the Climate Movement
description: The project uses Photovoice to highlight the lived experiences and narratives of youth climate organizers, aiming to make their impact visible beyond quantitative metrics and advocate for more equitable funding and evaluation practices. It seeks to influence funders and policymakers by centering justice, storytelling, and civic engagement.

title: The journey of an immigrant to Canada
description: This resource shares immigrants' stories to Canada, aiming to raise awareness of their migration reasons and celebrate community diversity, while fostering empathy towards immigrants.

title: Building Digital Learning Platforms for Afghan Women & Girls
description: This initiative empowers 100 Afghan women and girls by creating a centralized digital platform with free learning resources, business guides, and mentorship opportunities. Through accessible courses and interactive tools, it supports skill development, entrepreneurship, and long-term independence.

title: Youth Mental Health Awareness
description: The project aims to raise awareness of youth mental health by hosting a community event, such as a movie night, that both fosters connection and gathers insights into the challenges young people are facing. By collecting meaningful data and encouraging open dialogue, it seeks to inform solutions that support the well-being and healthy development of youth.

title: Universal Learning (ULearning): Empowering Immigrant Women Through Digital Literacy and Civic Engagement
description: ULearning empowers immigrant women in Ottawa by offering digital skill-building, confidence-boosting workshops, and online learning to foster community engagement and independence while addressing challenges such as language barriers and social isolation.

title: Health and Fitness Educational Website
description: The Health and Fitness Educational Website is hosting a two-day virtual launch to provide free expert resources on physical activity, nutrition, and mental wellness, aiming to empower at least 300 users with sustainable health habits. This initiative promotes public health literacy and civic engagement through accessible wellness education and interactive workshops.

title: The Future of Canada; What Canadians Think
description: The documentary "The Future of Canada: What Canadians Think" examines how immigration shapes Canada’s future, highlighting both challenges and opportunities related to integration and identity, while encouraging informed discussion and greater national unity.

title: TwinTalk Politics
description: TwinTalk Politics is a podcast that engages young Canadians in politics by featuring conversations on topics like lowering the voting age to 16 with Members of Parliament from across the country about issues that matter to youth. By making political discussions accessible, it aims to empower young voices and inspire greater participation in democracy.

title: Healthy Habits Live Weekend Workshop
description: The Healthy Habits Live Weekend Workshop was a two-day virtual event offering expert-led sessions on nutrition, physical activity, and stress management to equip participants with practical wellness tools, supporting CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation’s goal of fostering community resilience and civic engagement.

title: Cooperation in Global Governance: The Case of G20
description: The project measures cooperation on seven systemic issues within the G20, analyzes policy entrepreneurs' strategies, and offers a theoretical framework for understanding policymaking, ultimately aiming to help actors like Canada navigate geopolitical challenges and advocate for global public goods. It also seeks to enhance civic engagement and knowledge in international relations.

title: YouthCAN
description: YouthCAN is a digital platform that centralizes verified volunteer opportunities for teenagers in Greater Vancouver, making civic engagement more accessible and transparent. It aligns with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation to empower youth participation.

title: Empowering Afghan Women Entrepreneurs Through Business Workshops
description: This project supports the social and economic integration of Afghan refugees by providing language programs and creating opportunities for connection and collaboration. Through communication training and business networking, it helps refugees build skills, access employment, and engage with their new communities.

title: Crime Data Analysis 2014-2023
description: Police-reported crime is rising in Canada, raising concerns about its causes and effects, and this project provides an interactive dashboard analyzing crime data with demographic and economic factors to help identify trends and inform strategies for crime reduction and improved public safety.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Development Webinar Workshops
description: The Youth Entrepreneurship Development Webinar Workshops project provides underserved youth with expert-led online business training, empowering them to launch and grow enterprises, foster leadership, and contribute to sustainable economic and community development.

title: Lil Darlings Preschool “Cultural Connections” Initiative
description: This initiative creates an inclusive early learning environment that blends cultural traditions with global perspectives. It aims to foster curiosity, cultural awareness, and a strong foundation for children to grow into informed and engaged members of their community.

title: Financial Literacy Summit
description: The Financial Literacy Summit equips the Black community with essential money management skills through interactive workshops and expert discussions on topics like budgeting, investing, and credit. It also creates a lasting online resource library, making valuable financial knowledge accessible to a wider audience beyond the event.

title: Africville: A Community Displaced
description: The project aims to raise awareness about Africville’s history and the effects of systemic racism through a short documentary for schools and libraries, fostering civic engagement and accessible education, particularly for young people.

title: Making Connections and Supporting Integration:  Civic and Political Engagement Among Black Immigrants in Manitoba.
description: This research project explores the political experiences of black immigrants in Canada and recommend avenues to increase the opportunities and motivations to participate in political process by black immigrants in Manitoba.

title: History and Heritage Video Series
description: The History and Heritage Video Series project aims to explore and preserve the cultural heritage of local communities through engaging video storytelling. This initiative will feature four high-quality video episodes, including interviews with community members and historians, site visits to historical landmarks, and visuals of significant artifacts. By providing accessible educational content, the project seeks to foster greater appreciation for local history and traditions.

title: Sasher/Empowering Indigenous Youth Civic Engagement through Digital Storytelling and Environmental Advocacy
description: The Sasher project is a national networking platform for Indigenous youth to create a secure and inclusive digital environment for Indigenous youth throughout Canada to connect, learn, and contribute.

title: FBLA Ottawa
description: FBLA Ottawa is a Canadian student organization with 50 members that develops leadership and business skills through educational workshops, national conferences, and networking opportunities, preparing students for business careers.

title: Care for Change
description: This project expands a podcast by featuring interviews with Black, Indigenous, and Women of Color (BIWOC) professionals to explore and advocate for women’s health. It raises awareness of health disparities, shares practical insights, and fosters dialogue to support health equity and systemic change.

title: Fossil Free Research
description: Climate Justice UBC's Fossil Free Research campaign unites campus community members to end fossil fuel-funded research at UBC and promote real climate solutions, expanding its reach through events, education, and cross-department collaboration. The campaign builds on UBC's previous fossil fuel divestment success to foster deeper climate action.

title: Hygiene Awareness for Homelessness Initiative
description: This project is a digital platform to raise awareness about the hygiene challenges faced by homeless individuals in Canada and the related health risks. By educating the public, sharing resources, and encouraging community action, it promotes solutions and support to improve the well-being and dignity of homeless populations.

title: What is a Child and Youth Advocate?
