description: The project aims to create an independent Child and Youth Advocate in the Northwest Territories to address systemic abuse and neglect in the child welfare system, with a focus on Indigenous youth, by raising awareness, engaging youth, and coordinating advocacy to ensure accountability and systemic reform.

title: HarbourHacks
description: This project is a two-day hackathon and coding workshops for youth in Halifax to build a stronger in-person technology community. It aims to develop coding skills while raising awareness about cybersecurity, ethical technology use, and digital privacy, helping youth become more informed and responsible users of technology.

title: Green Jobs Media Series
description: The Green Jobs Media Series was a digital storytelling initiative that showcased diverse changemakers and addressed challenges faced by underrepresented youth in Canada's green economy, reaching over 18,500 people. It supported CANConnect and GLOCAL Foundation’s mission by promoting inclusive engagement, intergenerational dialogue, and youth leadership in sustainability.

title: Understanding the Canadian Economy through Economic Indicators
description: The project aims to boost economic literacy among young Canadians by teaching them about key economic indicators, encouraging critical analysis of policies, and fostering engaged, informed citizenship.

title: Soles4Souls Shoe Drive
description: This project redistributed gently used shoes to underserved communities to reduce waste, support local economies, and promote ethical aid. It engaged students in donation drives and volunteering, fostering community involvement and awareness of sustainable, responsible aid practices.

title: Link Up & Level Up (Afrikin Circle Networking Series 1)
description: Afrikin Circle supports African newcomer youth by offering mentorship, networking, and resource-sharing events to help them build connections, overcome isolation, and thrive in their new communities.

title: Stone Path Project
description: The Stone Path Project helps high school students navigate their transition by addressing challenges like mental health, academic pressure, and identity development. It provides support and tools to build confidence, resilience, and strong academic and social skills for long-term success.

title: Career Roadmap
description: The project helps newcomers—such as international students, immigrants, and refugees—navigate career opportunities and build supportive professional networks and community connections.

title: Sustainable Agriculture Practices Webinar Series
description: The Sustainable Agriculture Practices Webinar Series in March 2025 offered free, expert-led virtual education on environmentally responsible farming, helping farmers and communities address climate and soil challenges. The project promoted food security and climate adaptation by sharing practical knowledge and fostering community engagement through interactive webinars and resources.

title: Welcome to Canada: A Guide for Newcomers to Canada
description: The "Welcome to Canada" project offers a detailed guide to assist newcomers with essential information on immigration, culture, employment, healthcare, education, and settlement, aiming to ensure a smoother integration into Canadian society.

title: Gender Apartheid, Lack of Education for Women, Media Censorship, and the Role of Women in Afghanistan Under the Taliban's Dictatorship
description: The Fahim Dashty Foundation is hosting an event at the House of Commons in Ottawa to raise awareness about issues facing women in Afghanistan under the Taliban, including gender apartheid, lack of education, and media censorship. The event aims to highlight the impact of these challenges on freedom of expression and women’s roles in Afghan society.

title: Waste Management Info Hub
description: The project creates an interactive website featuring comprehensive data on waste across Canadian provinces to highlight concerns and promote awareness. Its goal is to encourage engagement among citizens, policymakers, and businesses in finding sustainable waste management solutions.

title: Youth Advocacy Live Stream Events
description: The Youth Advocacy Live Stream Events project offered interactive virtual sessions to teach advocacy skills and provide mentorship, empowering youth to become civically engaged leaders and take meaningful action in their communities.

title: MentorsRus
description: MentorsRus is a digital platform that employs an algorithm to connect IEHPs with Canadian mentors in the healthcare field. It encourages established Canadian healthcare professionals to open their networks and share industrial insights and knowledge to help IEHPs expedite integration into the healthcare system and foster a sense of belonging.

title: NaviGuide
description: This interactive digital product provides non-profits with knowledge, tools, and a structured framework to effectively adopt AI, aiming to reduce digital inequality and enhance operational efficiency and social impact.

title: Cybersecurity Live Streams for Families
description: The Cybersecurity Live Streams for Families project in March 2025 offered expert-led, interactive sessions and resources to help families learn practical digital safety strategies, promoting responsible online behavior and supporting digital literacy for civic engagement.

title: Newcomer Navigator
description: Newcomer Navigator is a civic education series designed to help newcomers to Canada, particularly from South Asia, gain the knowledge and understanding needed to engage with public institutions and participate in Canadian society.

title: Paths Unlocked
description: Paths Unlocked is a free online search directory designed to connect Canadians with 300+ diverse growth opportunities, lifelong learning spaces, and experiential learning. The platform focuses on providing easy access to internships, fellowships, leadership programs, cultural exchanges, and other development opportunities that foster personal and professional growth.

title: BIPOC Brunch Mentee-Mentor Mixer

title: Youth Advocacy Live Stream Events
description: The Youth Advocacy Live Stream Events project is a monthly live event series designed to empower young people to advocate for social change. Participants will engage in expert-led discussions, panel sessions, and interactive Q&A segments. This initiative aims to provide young people with the knowledge, tools, and inspiration needed to become active leaders in their communities and drive meaningful change.

title: Financial Independence for Youth
description: The Financial Independence for Youth event in March 2025 provided young people aged 16–25 with practical financial education through expert-led and interactive sessions, promoting economic stability and financial inclusion by equipping them with essential money management skills.

description: A two-day virtual event brought elders and youth together for storytelling sessions to share cultural histories and personal experiences, preserving oral traditions and promoting empathy, dialogue, and community engagement in alignment with CANConnect and the GLOCAL Foundation's goals.

description: The Community Anti-Car Theft Project aims to unite our neighborhood in a proactive approach to combat rising car theft rates. This initiative seeks to educate residents about preventive measures and foster a sense of collective responsibility. By hosting online webinars, we intend to share resources, strategies, and personal experiences, ultimately empowering community members to safeguard their vehicles and reduce crime.

title: Technology for the Greater Good

It promotes inclusive education, social awareness, and civic engagement, enabling youth to use technology for positive community change.

title: Balancing the Scales: Gender Representation in Canada's Federal Politics
description: The project examines gender representation in Canadian federal politics, revealing both progress and persistent barriers to women's participation. Through data-driven visuals, it seeks to inform citizens and encourage discussion and advocacy for increased gender equity in governance.

title: Dreaming of Alternative Food Futures

title: Women in Leadership Podcast Interviews

By amplifying diverse perspectives, this project promotes gender equality and empowerment in leadership roles, contributing to positive societal change.

title: The Collection Y.E.O. - Youth Enrichment Opportunities
description: The Collection Y.E.O. website provides a curated database of 100 enrichment opportunities in diverse fields for Canadian high school students, accessible both in-person and online. description: Tag4Access is an app that crowdsources and verifies accessibility information in Nova Scotia to promote inclusion and civic engagement.

title: Newcomer Health Compass
description: The project guides newcomer families in Ontario through the healthcare system with multilingual resources, improving access, understanding, and community engagement.

title: The Knight Owls Robotics Team
description: The Knight Owls Robotics Team is a student-led group that builds robots for the 2026 FIRST Robotics Competition while fostering leadership, STEAM skills, and community engagement through mentorship and hands-on learning.

title: Mapping Winnipeg
description: The project enhances access to Winnipeg’s history by using an interactive website that links street names to their origins through archival research and community involvement.

title: Nursing Without Borders
description: The project empowers internationally educated nurses in Canada by providing mentorship, workshops, and peer support to overcome barriers and promote equity and inclusion in healthcare.

title: Faces of Change: Youth Voices Against Racism (Pilot Documentary & Community Dialogue)
description: The project showcases grassroots organizations and leaders driving social change, using storytelling to raise awareness, foster youth engagement, and promote inclusion and equity.

title: Stay or Return? Legal Navigation Guide for Syrian Nationals in Canada
description: The project provides an accessible legal guide for Syrian nationals in Canada, simplifying immigration rules to help newcomers understand refugee status, residency obligations, and travel, thereby enabling informed decision-making.

title: Empowering Ribbons
description: “Empowering Ribbons” is a youth-led initiative that donates handmade ribbon skirts to support Indigenous women in shelters, fostering cultural reconnection, healing, and awareness of the impacts of colonization.

title: Healthy Aging Initiative: Tamil Dementia Awareness and Community Engagement
description: This youth-led initiative advances dementia awareness and healthy aging among Tamil-speaking older adults and caregivers in the Greater Toronto Area by providing culturally relevant outreach, bilingual workshops, resource translation, and youth mentorship in health equity and education.

title: Community Connections Workshop
description: The Community Connections Workshop empowers high school students in the Northwest Territories to overcome challenges and build practical skills through resume-building, speaker workshops, and a career fair connecting them with local opportunities and support systems.

title: Growing Older, Living Deeply (GOLD) Poetry Project
description: The GOLD Poetry Project combats ageism in Canada by empowering older adults to share original poetry about aging, fostering intergenerational understanding and dialogue through a national digital platform and public anthology.

title: Waking Hours
description: Waking Hours is a short film that delves into identity, cultural resilience, and the challenges faced by minority communities in Canada, aiming to promote reflection on multiculturalism and representation.

title: The English Launchpad
description: The English Launchpad is a free, mobile-friendly platform that helps newcomers and adult immigrants in Canada improve practical English skills for daily life, focusing on healthcare, employment, and civic participation to reduce language barriers and boost community engagement.

title: Misinformation and Democratic Participation: Kenyan-Canadian Immigrant Experiences
description: The project analyzes how misinformation circulating in digital networks affects the political views and democratic involvement of Kenyan-Canadian immigrants, aiming to understand its impact on immigrant communities and democracy in Canada.

title: Growing Food Security: Indoor Gardening with Aqsarniit Green Club
description: In Iqaluit, fresh produce is expensive and hard to access due to transportation costs and environmental limits. This student-led project tackled that directly using hydroponics, grow lights, and window garden beds to grow food indoors at Aqsarniit Middle School. Students built practical skills in indoor food production, supported a school snack program with fresh harvest, and shared seedlings with a local greenhouse — extending the project's impact into the wider community.

title: Chess for Hope
description: Chess for Hope is a youth-led initiative in Regina that empowers students and builds inclusive school communities through mentoring, chess club development, and student-led events that promote leadership, connection, and civic engagement.

title: The Collective Closet
description: The Collective Closet fosters sustainability and community by hosting clothing swaps that reduce waste, promote social connection, and encourage civic engagement around issues like fast fashion and environmental responsibility.

title: Crafting Kinship
description: This virtual workshop empowers Indigenous participants to create ceremonial rattles and learn about sound-based healing, fostering cultural revitalization, community wellness, and intergenerational knowledge-sharing through accessible art bundles and Elder guidance.

title: Cultures in Conversation: Conversations on Land, History, and Belonging
description: Cultures in Conversation is a community-based project fostering dialogue and civic engagement to help newcomers to Canada understand Indigenous Peoples, reconciliation, and their roles within Canadian society.

title: The Great Trek for Transit
description: The Great Trek for Transit is a student-led advocacy campaign mobilizing community support and civic engagement for extending SkyTrain service to UBC’s Vancouver campus to advance sustainable and accessible public transit.

title: Dancing Forward Nunavut Program
description: Indigenous communities in Nunavut are fly-in only, limiting access to sports and arts for youth. Dancing Forward partners with local governments to bring free dance programs — jazz, hip hop, acro, ballet, and modern — to these communities with no application process or fees. Expecting 50 youth (ages 5–13) each week, participants receive 15+ hours of instruction, performance experience, and a certificate of achievement, while also gaining cultural insights and celebrating the diversity of dance styles.

title: NEOS: A Community Platform That Connects and Empowers Students and Newcomers Across Canada
description: NEOS is a youth-led initiative in Canada that empowers students and newcomers through accessible resources, peer support, and community engagement opportunities.

title: The CARES Project
description: The CARES Project enhances healthcare access for newcomer families by pairing them with trained university student volunteers who provide navigation, interpretation, and support in understanding medical information and health systems.

title: Bridging Language Barriers in Healthcare: A Bilingual Mandarin–English Medical Terminology Guide for Community Access
description: This project creates a bilingual Mandarin–English medical terminology pamphlet to help Mandarin-speaking immigrants navigate Canada’s healthcare system by improving health literacy, reducing medication errors, and enhancing patient–provider communication.

title: Little St. Nick Foundation Queen’s
description: The Little St. Nick Foundation Queen’s chapter is a student-led program that reduces pediatric patient anxiety at Kingston Health Sciences Centre by delivering personalized comfort gift bags, distributing over 500 bags, and engaging more than 3,000 community members in meaningful acts of care.

title: The Find Your Way Database
description: The Find Your Way Database is an online platform that connects at-risk and unhoused youth to personalized shelters and support services, offering real-time availability, inclusive searches, and early access through school partnerships to reduce barriers to care.

title: Queer Ecology Hikes
description: Queer Ecology Hikes are inclusive, community walks that foster mindful, consensual, and reflective connections with nature and each other, emphasizing care and learning over extraction or performance.

title: Building Belonging Through the Bridging of Worlds
description: Watch as students from the High Arctic region of Nunavut witness Trees and tall buildings for the First Time!

title: Can You See the Difference? Microgreens — The Context Engine
description: A 5-month classroom initiative at a Nunavut school using microgreens and sprouts to build scientific curiosity, agency, and environmental understanding in students. The project harnesses 'salience' — contrast, timing, and meaningful context — to make learning stick: students watch visible change happen within a single school day, from brown seedlings to green growth they caused and cared for themselves.

title: Garden and Music Wellness Program
description: A dual-focus wellness program pairing indoor gardening with piano instruction for Nunavut students. Through consistent plant care and musical practice, youth build responsibility, focus, patience, and confidence. Students develop foundational piano skills, maintain a garden kit of their own, and grow through shared performances and a thriving classroom garden.

title: Kool Runnings Dog Sled Youth Program
description: A Nunavut youth program for ages 10–15 centred on traditional Inuit dog sledding culture. Young volunteers learn to feed and care for sled dogs, build knowledge of Inuit traditions, and develop responsibility and an appreciation for sustainable northern living — connecting cultural heritage with hands-on practice.

title: Promoting Iqaluit Community Greenhouse Kids and Youth Program
description: An outreach initiative to grow youth participation at the Iqaluit Community Greenhouse through hands-on workshops in planting, worm composting, and sustainable gardening. Using plant kits, seed kits, and composting supplies, the program connects youth to food systems and environmental stewardship while building community through shared green spaces.

title: Purple Cup Community and Regional Volleyball Tournament
description: A multi-community volleyball tournament held in Kugaaruk, Nunavut, bringing together teams from across the region for four days of competition, cultural exchange, and community spirit. The Purple Cup supports youth leadership, volunteer development, and inter-community connection through sport — with logistics spanning team travel, refereeing, facility setup, meals, and awards.

title: Youth Carving
description: A Nunavut youth initiative supporting the practice and preservation of traditional Inuit carving. Young participants receive materials, mentorship, and dedicated space to develop artistic skills while deepening their connection to Inuit cultural heritage and intergenerational knowledge.

title: Decolonizing Politics
description: This presentation examines how Six Nations land governance conflicts reveal ongoing settler colonial power structures, showing that true decolonization requires moving beyond compensation and consultation toward Indigenous sovereignty, consent, and land-based self-determination.

title: Lying Through Their Teeth
description: Lying Through Their Teeth examines how social media, AI-generated content, and weak digital literacy have allowed misinformation to spread rapidly in Canada, undermining public trust, civic responsibility, and the ability to separate fact from manipulation.

title: Municipal Data Collection and Compiling
description: An intern team compiled a comprehensive Canadian municipal dataset using Statistics Canada data and Python, covering demographics, immigration, visible minorities, language, and labour force characteristics across most Canadian municipalities for the 2021 census year.
